newsitem.title: USA: Blue-chip stocks extend comeback to third session.
newsitem.headline: Blue-chip stocks extend comeback to third session.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks romped ahead for the third straight session Tuesday, clawing back on bargain hunting after last week's rout and with the help of another rally in technology shares.
The Dow Jones industrial average closed up 53.25 points at 6,609.16, having so far regained more than 130 points from last week's sell-off of 215 points.
In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 1,338 to 1,108 on active volume of 448 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
"I think folks are looking at prices, thinking they're reasonably attractive, and stepping up a little bit," said Robert von Pentz, a managing partner at Columbia Partners.
Technology stocks again led the recovery. The tech-heavy Nasdaq composite rose 6.02 points to 1,257.37, its fourth straight advance.
Analysts said technology stocks, particularily semiconductor makers, got a boost from stronger-than-expected quarterly earnings from Motorola Inc. and Advanced Micro Devices Inc.
They also cited positive comments on the group from Goldman Sachs strategist Abby Joseph Cohen.

In a call to the firm's investors, Cohen said the market correction was over, and the Standard & Poor's 500 stock index was likely to end the year at 850, up from its recent record closing high of 816.29. On Tuesday, the S&P ended at 766.12, up 3.99 points.
"This has been a very dramatic period for the U.S. financial markets, but we remain optimistic about the U.S. market outlook," Cohen said.

"We believe the U.S. economy is nowhere near recession, inflation is under very good control, and we are making no change in our asset allocation. We are comfortable with our year-end price targets," she said.
Among individual stocks, Motorola ended off 1-5/8 at 59-1/2 after rising prior to the release late Monday of the earnings report. Advanced Micro rose 3/8 to 43-3/8.
Among other technology stocks, Texas Instruments Inc. rose 3-1/2 to 88-7/8, Microsoft Corp. added 2-3/8 to 98-1/4, and Dell Computer Corp. gained 5 to 78-3/4.

Stocks moved higher despite a weak Treasury market, where the 30-year bond was off 12/32 in late trading, sending its yield up to 7.10 percent from Monday's close at 7.07 percent. The bond's price and yield move in opposite directions.

While stock market trading in the past weeks has been dominated by concern over rising interest rates, first quarter earnings reports will be the focus of Wall Street in the coming sessions, analysts said.
"From now on it looks like it's going to depend on earnings," said Harry Laubscher, an analyst at Tucker Anthony.
Bank stocks, also featured by Goldman's Cohen, rallied. Citicorp rose 2-3/4 to 114-3/4, J.P. Morgan & Co. Inc. gained 2-1/8 to 101-3/8 and Chase Manhattan Corp. added 2-5/8 to 96-7/8.
Viking Office Products Inc. sank 5-1/2 to 14-1/2 after forecasting that results for the latest quarter would be below Wall Street estimates.
Transocean Offshore Inc. gained 2-3/4 to 61-5/8. The company said it had received letters-of-intent to contract two of its deepwater drilling rigs.
The American Stock Exchange index rose 0.98 to 561.42.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks rose 1.63 to 402.31. The average share was up 17 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was 7,305.75, up 32.758 or 0.45 percent.
